content.title: About
content.content: Head cheese is a traditional meat jelly made from boiled meat, natural gelatin, and spices that sets into a firm slice. It is usually prepared from beef, pork, or poultry, often with bones, cartilage and skin to provide gelatin. Served cold, sliced, and commonly accompanied by mustard or vinegar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Head cheese is known worldwide under various names: aspic (France), meat jelly (Germany), galareta (Poland).
It is traditionally made in colder months when ambient temperature helps the jelly set quickly.
In Soviet cuisine, head cheese was a staple for holidays such as New Year and Victory Day.
For a clear jelly, only a clean, fat‑free broth is used.
Some regional recipes add carrots, onions, garlic and spices for extra flavor.

items.title: Rich in collagen
items.content: Collagen from bones and cartilage supports skin elasticity, joint health, and connective tissue.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: The meat provides a complete set of essential amino acids for tissue repair and growth.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Contains iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Head cheese fits well into low‑carb diets as it contains virtually no sugar.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The broth component helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Insufficiently cooked broth may harbor pathogens; proper heating and handling are essential.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Excessive salt can make head cheese unsuitable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to certain types of meat.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of gelatin can cause stomach upset in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve head cheese cold, sliced into thin pieces. It is often paired with mustard, vinegar, horseradish or fresh herbs. It can be accompanied by boiled vegetables or potatoes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep head cheese refrigerated, covered with plastic wrap or in an airtight container, for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size pieces, though the texture may change slightly after thawing.
